# svelte-whisper

> Tiny runtime i18n for Svelte 5 single-page apps, built on runes. Locale files load on demand. About 1.8 kB gzipped, no dependencies beyond Svelte, no extra build plugin. Client-side only: it keeps state in the module, so do not use it for server-side rendering.

Requires `svelte@^5.9.0`. Install with `npm install github:Shilo/svelte-whisper`. The package is a runes module (`index.svelte.js`) that the app's Svelte plugin compiles.

## Recommended setup

```js
// src/main.js
import { mount } from 'svelte';
import { init, registerLoader } from 'svelte-whisper';
import App from './App.svelte';

registerLoader(import.meta.glob('./locales/*.json')); // file name = locale id, one lazy chunk each
await init({ fallback: 'en', persistKey: 'my-app-locale' });
mount(App, { target: document.getElementById('app') });
```

```svelte
<script>
    import { t, getLocale, setLocale, getLocales, localeName, formatNumber } from 'svelte-whisper';
    let { count, total } = $props();
    const title = $derived(t('nav.settings'));
</script>

<h1>{t('greeting', { name: 'Ada' })}</h1>
<p>{t('cart.items', { count })} · {formatNumber(total, { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' })}</p>
<select value={getLocale()} onchange={async e => { const s = e.currentTarget; if (!await setLocale(s.value)) s.value = getLocale(); }}>
    {#each getLocales() as id}<option value={id}>{localeName(id)}</option>{/each}
</select>
```

## Rules for writing code with it

- First check whether the component is a legacy one, meaning it uses `export let`, `$:`, `$$props` or `$$restProps`, or runes are switched off for it (`<svelte:options runes={false} />`, or `runes: false` in the compiler options). If not, call the functions: `t('key')`, `getLocale()`. In a legacy component Svelte only follows stores, so write `$t('key')` and `$locale` (both are exported as stores too) and pass the locale to formatters: `formatNumber(n, options, $locale)`. `$t` and `$locale` also work in every other component. `tr()` was 1.x and does not exist.
- `t('key', vars)` is the only translate function. Use it in markup, `<script>`, `$derived`, `$effect`, event handlers and plain `.js`/`.ts` modules. It is reactive: callers inside markup, `$derived` or `$effect` re-run when the locale or a dictionary changes. It always returns a string: the key itself when the key is missing everywhere. List items are addressed by index (`rules.0`).
- Keys are dotted paths into nested JSON: `nav.settings.title`.
- Placeholders: `{name}` with an object, `{0}` with an array. Unmatched placeholders stay visible.
- Plurals: the dictionary value is an object keyed by `Intl.PluralRules` category (`one`, `few`, `many`, `other`, …) or an exact number (`"0"`); pass a numeric `count`. Always include `other`.
- Never build a sentence by joining translated fragments. One sentence, one key.
- Format with `formatNumber(value, intlOptions?, locale?)` and `formatDate(value, intlOptions?, locale?)`; never bare `toLocaleString()` or `toFixed()`. Percentages are `formatPercent(value, precision?, locale?)`. Both follow the active locale and are reactive.
- `localeName(id)` returns a language's own name (`ja` → `日本語`); do not add translation keys for language names.
- `getLocale()` reads the active locale (reactive). `setLocale(id)` switches: resolves `true` when active, `false` if the load failed or a newer switch won. `loadLocale(id)` preloads. `resetLocale()` forgets the stored choice.
- `init` chooses the starting locale: stored choice (`persistKey`) → browser language (`detect`, default on) → `initial` → `fallback`. Only explicit `setLocale` calls are stored.
- The library sets `<html lang>` and `dir`; do not do it by hand.
- `addDictionary(id, dict)` adds translations already in memory (bundled main language, tests).
- With no loaders registered, a locale is fetched from `{base}locales/{id}.json`.
- A key missing from the active locale falls back to the fallback locale and is reported once: `init({ onMissing({ locale, key }) {} })`, else `console.warn`. In Vite dev mode a dev overlay lists them; it is never in production builds.
- Typed keys: augment `Register` with `dictionary: typeof en` in a `.d.ts` file (`declare module 'svelte-whisper'`).

## Exports

`init`, `registerLoader`, `addDictionary`, `loadLocale`, `setLocale`, `resetLocale`, `getLocale`, `getLocales`, `detectLocale`, `localeName`, `t`, `locale`, `formatNumber`, `formatPercent`, `formatDate`. Types: `WhisperOptions`, `WhisperKey`, `WhisperVars`, `WhisperDictionary`, `WhisperLoader`, `Translate`, `MissingKeyEntry`, `Register`.

## Locale tools

`npx svelte-whisper check` reports missing and extra keys and placeholder mismatches in every locale, and exits 1 on errors. With `--usage src` it also scans the code as text and reports unused keys and undefined ones (a literal key in `t(` or `$t(` that has no message; these also exit 1). `diff --since <ref>` lists changed source strings. `apply <locale> <file>` merges translations and rewrites the locale in source order. `sync` drops stale keys. Add `--json` for machine-readable output.

When translating or auditing locale files, follow the skills instead of editing whole JSON files by hand:

- [whisper-setup](skills/whisper-setup/SKILL.md): add the library to an app, extract hard-coded text
- [whisper-translate](skills/whisper-translate/SKILL.md): translate new and changed strings, add a language
- [whisper-audit](skills/whisper-audit/SKILL.md): find missing, unused and broken translations
